dossier.public_summary: The 0.65-day dip is on the target M dwarf but shows a clear secondary eclipse (~1200 ppm, 16% of primary), large out-of-eclipse variation, and a period identical to the star's 0.65-day rotation with huge spot amplitudes. Depth varies by 76% between TESS sectors and the transit is much longer than a central planet transit would be, all pointing to a stellar companion or spotted binary, not a planet.

reasons.why: A secondary dip at 0.795 phase with depth ~16% of the 7336 ppm primary is seen at SNR 10.11 well above best_brightening_snr 43.86 excess, inconsistent with a planet and expected for a stellar companion (hot EB / ellipsoidal).

Large out-of-eclipse modulation nearly as large as the eclipse with very high chi2 indicates a close binary phase curve/ellipsoidal variation, not a quiet planet environment. Variability chi2_dof 146.2 supports live stellar variability.

The 0.654-d dip period is exactly the star's spot rotation period (period_d 0.653-0.654 in all 5 sectors amplitude_ppm 18176-26474) at a 1:1 multiple; combined with a transit duration ratio 1.751 vs central_h 0.7114 and star_density_penalty 5901, this favors variability/sectoring of a rotating spotted low-mass star over a planet.

Depth varies strongly with sector: 5013 ppm to 10365 ppm (76% change) with p_constant_all 9.62e-06 and per-source p_constant 0.000311 and 0.00108, indicating real astrophysical/eclipsing variability, not a stable planetary transit.
Difference image is consistent with on-target (on none of the neighbours), ruling out a blended neighbour eclipse but not a binary on the target itself, which the secondary and phase curve favour.
